application.name: My Thai Star
application.description: A full-stack reference restaurant management application built on the Devon4j/devonfw framework, demonstrating best practices across Angular frontend, Java Spring Boot backend, and Node.js NestJS backend.
application.purpose: Serves as a reference application to demonstrate modern enterprise application development patterns including REST APIs, JWT security, two-factor authentication, role-based access control, email notifications, table reservation management, order processing, ML-based demand prediction, and customer clustering.

technical_stack.frontend: Angular 11+ with NgRx state management, Angular Material UI, Transloco i18n, Service Workers (PWA)
technical_stack.backend_java: Devon4j / Spring Boot 2.4.4, JAX-RS REST, Spring Security, Hibernate JPA, H2/SAP HANA
technical_stack.backend_node: NestJS (Node.js), TypeORM, Passport JWT, Swagger/OpenAPI, Winston logging

architecture_patterns: Repository pattern (Spring Data JPA / TypeORM custom repositories)

files.summary: Core business logic for all booking lifecycle operations including creation, confirmation, cancellation, and guest invitation management.
files.description: Manages the complete booking lifecycle for the restaurant. Handles creation of common table reservations and group invitation events, generates unique MD5-based booking tokens, sets expiration dates (booking date minus 1 hour), sends email confirmations to hosts and invitations to guests, and manages the cancellation workflow including cascading guest order deletions. Supports two booking modes: COMMON (single party reservation) and INVITED (group event with invited guests).
business_rules: Booking token is generated using MD5 hash of email + date + time, prefixed with 'CB_' for common bookings
Guest invitation tokens are prefixed with 'GB_'
Booking expiration date is set to booking date minus 1 hour
Booking creation date is set to current timestamp
New bookings are initialized with canceled=false
When a booking is deleted, all associated orders are deleted first (cascade delete)
When a guest is deleted, all associated guest orders are deleted first
Cancellation of an invite requires a valid booking token and must be within the cancellation time limit
When a guest accepts an invite, their accepted status is set to true and confirmation emails are sent to both host and guest
When a guest declines an invite, all guest orders are deleted and acceptance is set to false
Confirmation email to host includes booking token, date, guest list, and cancellation link
Invitation email to guests includes accept and decline links using guest token
Assistants count must be at minimum 1 (validated by @Min annotation)
Assistants count must be at most 2 digits (no decimal places)

parameters: id (Long): Primary key of the booking
method_breakdown.returns: BookingCto: Composite Transfer Object with booking, table, order, invited guests
method_breakdown.significance: Core read operation for booking data

method_breakdown.summary: Creates a new booking with token generation, expiration date calculation, invited guest setup, and email notifications
parameters: booking (BookingCto): Booking details and list of invited guests
method_breakdown.returns: BookingEto: Created booking entity transfer object with generated ID
method_breakdown.significance: Primary booking creation entry point with full workflow including email notifications

method_breakdown.summary: Deletes a booking and all associated orders via cascade
parameters: bookingId (Long): ID of booking to delete
method_breakdown.returns: boolean: true if deletion succeeded
method_breakdown.significance: Ensures referential integrity by deleting orders before the booking

method_breakdown.summary: Marks an invited guest's status as accepted and sends confirmation emails to both host and guest
method_breakdown.returns: InvitedGuestEto: Updated invited guest record
method_breakdown.significance: Manages the guest acceptance workflow

method_breakdown.summary: Marks a guest as declined, deletes any guest orders, and notifies host
method_breakdown.returns: InvitedGuestEto: Updated invited guest record with accepted=false
method_breakdown.significance: Handles guest rejection workflow including order cleanup

method_breakdown.summary: Cancels an entire booking by token, deletes all guests and orders, validates cancellation time window
method_breakdown.returns: void
method_breakdown.significance: Full booking cancellation with cascading cleanup and notification

method_breakdown.summary: Generates a unique token for a booking or guest using MD5 hash of email and timestamp
parameters: email (String): Email of host or guest
method_breakdown.returns: String: Formatted token with prefix + date + MD5 hash
method_breakdown.significance: Security-critical token generation used for authorization of booking operations

files.summary: Core business logic for order processing including creation, validation, cancellation, and dish ordering statistics.
files.description: Manages the complete order lifecycle including order creation with token validation, order line processing with dish extras, cancellation time-window enforcement, and email confirmations with itemized pricing. Validates that orders are associated with valid bookings or accepted guests and prevents duplicate orders per booking. Also provides analytics on ordered dishes per day and per month.
business_rules: Orders must be associated with a valid booking token starting with 'CB_' (common) or 'GB_' (guest)
Invalid token prefix throws WrongTokenException
Common bookings (CB_) require an existing valid booking; if not found, throws NoBookingException
Guest bookings (GB_) require an existing accepted invited guest; if not found, throws NoInviteException
Only one order is allowed per booking or per invited guest (OrderAlreadyExistException)
Order cancellation is only allowed if current time is before the cancellation limit (booking date minus hoursLimit hours)
CancelNotAllowedException is thrown if cancellation window has expired
Order confirmation email is sent after order creation with itemized dish costs and extras
Email includes a cancellation link using the order ID
Order total price includes dish base price multiplied by quantity plus selected extras prices
Order line extras are deduplicated using a HashSet before price calculation
Default pageable falls back to pageNumber=1, pageSize=5 if not provided

method_breakdown.summary: Creates an order with full validation: token type check, booking/guest existence, duplicate check, then persists order and lines
parameters: order (OrderCto): Order composite object with booking token and order lines
method_breakdown.returns: OrderEto: Saved order entity transfer object
method_breakdown.significance: Primary order creation method with full validation workflow

method_breakdown.summary: Validates cancellation window then deletes order lines and order record
parameters: orderId (Long): ID of the order to delete
method_breakdown.returns: boolean: true if deletion was successful
method_breakdown.significance: Enforces time-based cancellation policy

method_breakdown.summary: Validates token type and ensures booking/guest exists and has no existing order
method_breakdown.returns: OrderEntity: Validated order entity with booking/guest IDs set
method_breakdown.significance: Central validation step preventing duplicate orders and unauthorized order creation

method_breakdown.summary: Determines booking type based on token prefix (CB_ or GB_)
parameters: token (String): the booking or guest token
method_breakdown.returns: BookingType: COMMON or INVITED enum value
method_breakdown.significance: Token routing logic that determines order processing path

method_breakdown.summary: Checks if the current time is before the cancellation deadline (booking date minus configured hours)
method_breakdown.returns: boolean: true if cancellation is still allowed
method_breakdown.significance: Time-gate business rule enforcement for cancellation policy

method_breakdown.summary: Retrieves analytics data on ordered dishes filtered by DAILY or MONTHLY granularity
method_breakdown.returns: Page<OrderedDishesCto>: Paginated list of ordered dish statistics
method_breakdown.significance: Management reporting on dish popularity and demand patterns

files.summary: Business logic for managing dishes, categories, and ingredients including image handling and category-based filtering.
files.description: Manages the restaurant's menu catalog including dish creation and retrieval, category management, ingredient management, and dish image handling. Supports multi-category filtering and Base64 image encoding for frontend consumption. Provides paginated search with category filter post-processing to support multi-tag dish filtering.
business_rules: Dish images are converted to Base64 encoded strings for API response
Category filtering is applied post-query to support multi-category dish lookup (a dish matching any selected category is included)
Duplicate dishes are excluded when matching multiple categories
Dishes can belong to multiple categories (many-to-many relationship)
Dishes can have multiple optional extras (ingredients) with individual prices
Default page size falls back to pageNumber=0 if pageable is null

method_breakdown.summary: Retrieves paginated dish list with images, categories, and extras, applying optional category filters
parameters: criteria (DishSearchCriteriaTo): Search terms, categories, price/likes filters, pagination
method_breakdown.returns: Page<DishCto>: Paginated dish composite objects with images and extras
method_breakdown.significance: Main dish browsing API used by the restaurant menu page

method_breakdown.summary: Retrieves a single dish by ID with all related categories, image, and extras
method_breakdown.returns: DishCto: Full dish composite object
method_breakdown.significance: Used for detailed dish view and order line construction

method_breakdown.summary: Filters dish list to include only those matching at least one of the selected category IDs
method_breakdown.returns: List<DishCto>: Filtered dish list
method_breakdown.significance: Implements the multi-category dish filtering business rule

method_breakdown.summary: Returns dishes filtered by a specific category name
method_breakdown.returns: Page<DishCto>: Paginated dishes matching the category
method_breakdown.significance: Supports category-based menu browsing

files.summary: User management including registration, authentication support, two-factor authentication, and role management.
files.description: Manages user accounts for the restaurant system including user registration with password encoding, duplicate username prevention, two-factor authentication (2FA) setup via TOTP/QR codes, and role-based user profile management. Integrates with Spring Security for credential handling and supports manager, waiter, and customer roles.
business_rules: Username must be unique - attempting to save a user with an existing username throws UserAlreadyExistsException
Passwords are encoded using Spring's PasswordEncoder before storage (never stored in plain text)
Default userRoleId is set to 0 if not provided during registration
Two-factor authentication is optional and can be enabled/disabled per user
TOTP secret is randomly generated (Base32) the first time a QR code is requested, if not already set
QR code is only generated if the user has two-factor authentication enabled
User role maps to one of three roles: Manager, Waiter, or Customer

method_breakdown.summary: Registers a new user with password encoding and duplicate username validation
parameters: user (UserEto): User details including username, password, roleId
method_breakdown.returns: UserEto: Created user entity transfer object
method_breakdown.significance: User registration entry point with security enforcement

method_breakdown.summary: Generates a TOTP QR code for 2FA setup, initializing secret if not already set
parameters: username (String): Username for QR code generation
method_breakdown.returns: UserQrCodeTo: QR code data including secret and image
method_breakdown.significance: Enables two-factor authentication setup for users

method_breakdown.summary: Enables or disables two-factor authentication for a specific user
parameters: user (UserEto): User with updated twoFactorStatus flag
method_breakdown.returns: UserEto: Updated user entity
method_breakdown.significance: Controls 2FA feature toggle per user account

method_breakdown.summary: Loads user profile with role for Spring Security authorization
method_breakdown.returns: UserProfile: Profile containing user ID and role
method_breakdown.significance: Bridge between user management and Spring Security authorization

files.summary: ML-based next-week dish demand prediction using SAP HANA PAL (Predictive Analytics Library) ARIMA models.
files.description: Implements demand forecasting for restaurant dishes using the Auto-ARIMA time series model from SAP HANA's Predictive Analytics Library. The system trains models on historical order data with weather temperature and holiday flags as covariates, then generates 7-day forecasts for each dish. Predictions inform restaurant inventory and staffing decisions.
business_rules: Predictions are generated per dish for the next 7 days
Training data includes temperature and holiday information as covariates for each forecast day
Model retraining is skipped if training data already exists for the given dish and start date (idempotent)
Training is skipped if no historical data exists
Old forecast data is deleted before each new prediction run
ARIMA model is estimated using PAL_AUTOARIMA stored procedure
Forecast is generated using PAL_ARIMA_FORECAST stored procedure
Only accessible to users with MANAGER role (PERMISSION_FIND_NEXT_WEEK_PREDICTION)
technical_libraries: SAP HANA PAL (via JPA native query)

method_breakdown.summary: Generates 7-day demand forecast for all dishes using ARIMA models trained on historical data
parameters: criteria (PredictionSearchCriteriaTo): Start date, temperatures, holidays per day
method_breakdown.returns: PredictionDataTo: List of daily dish demand predictions
method_breakdown.significance: Core analytics feature for restaurant demand planning

files.summary: Geo-spatial customer clustering analysis using k-means or similar clustering algorithms via named query.
files.description: Provides geographic clustering of customer booking data by dish and date range for market analysis. Uses a database-level named query to perform k-means clustering, returning cluster assignments for bookings. Enables the restaurant to identify geographic customer segments and hotspots.
business_rules: Clustering is performed per dish and time window (start/end booking dates)
Number of clusters (k) is configurable per request
Only accessible to users with MANAGER role (PERMISSION_FIND_GEO_CLUSTER)

method_breakdown.summary: Executes geo-spatial customer clustering query for a specific dish within a date range
method_breakdown.returns: ClustersDataCto: Clustered booking data with cluster assignments
method_breakdown.significance: Market intelligence feature for customer geographic analysis

files.summary: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) configuration defining permissions and role groups for the application.
files.description: Defines all fine-grained permissions and role groups for the application's security model. Three roles are defined: Waiter (can find orders and bookings), Manager (can find bookings, orders, predictions, and geo clusters), and Customer (can find bookings and orders). All CRUD permissions are prefixed with 'mts.'
business_rules: WAITER role has permissions: FindOrder, FindBooking
MANAGER role has permissions: FindBooking, FindOrder, GetNextWeekPrediction, GetGeoCluster
CUSTOMER role has permissions: FindBooking, FindOrder
Permission naming convention: mts.<Action><Entity> (e.g., mts.FindOrder)
Admin group is available for full access control

files.summary: Spring Security UserDetailsService implementation that loads user credentials and authorities from the database.
files.description: Bridges the Spring Security authentication framework with the application's user management. Loads user credentials by username, maps the user's role to granted authorities via the access control framework, and returns a UserData object for the authentication provider.
business_rules: Authentication fails with UsernameNotFoundException if user does not exist or any error occurs
User authorities are derived from the access control group tree for the user's role
Undefined access control IDs are logged as warnings but do not block authentication

method_breakdown.summary: Loads user by username, resolves role-based authorities, returns Spring Security UserDetails
method_breakdown.returns: UserDetails: Spring Security user details with credentials and authorities
method_breakdown.significance: Critical security method called on every login attempt

files.summary: NestJS use case for creating bookings with table auto-assignment and email notifications.
files.description: Implements the booking creation workflow in a transactional context. For COMMON bookings, automatically assigns a free table based on the number of assistants and booking date/time. For INVITED bookings, creates invited guest records. Validates that common bookings do not have invited guests and that free tables are available before proceeding.
business_rules: COMMON bookings cannot have invited guests (throws InvalidBookingException)
COMMON bookings require a free table with seats >= assistants count
If no free table is available, throws NoFreeTablesException
Table availability check window is: booking date minus 1 hour to booking date
INVITED bookings support multiple invited guests with individual guest tokens
Booking token format: 'CB_' + date + '_' + md5(email + timestamp)
Expiration date is set to booking date minus 1 hour
Creation date is set to current timestamp
Booking type defaults to COMMON if not specified
All operations run within a single database transaction
Email notifications are sent asynchronously after booking creation

method_breakdown.summary: Creates a booking transactionally: validates type, assigns table for common bookings, persists invited guests, sends emails
method_breakdown.returns: Promise<Booking>: Created booking entity
method_breakdown.significance: Core booking creation entry point with transactional guarantee

files.summary: NestJS use case for creating orders with token validation, guest acceptance check, and pricing.
files.description: Implements order creation with full token validation and business rule enforcement. Validates booking tokens (CB_/GB_), checks guest acceptance status for invited bookings, prevents duplicate orders per booking/guest, persists order and order lines with extras, calculates total price, and sends order confirmation email.
business_rules: Booking token must start with 'CB_' (common) or 'GB_' (invited guest); otherwise throws InvalidTokenException
For CB_ tokens: booking must exist; throws InvalidTokenException if not found
For CB_ tokens: booking must not already have an order; throws OrderAlreadyDoneException
For GB_ tokens: invited guest must exist; throws InvalidTokenException if not found
For GB_ tokens: invited guest must have accepted the invitation; throws GuestNotAcceptedException
For GB_ tokens: invited guest must not already have an order; throws OrderAlreadyDoneException
Total price = sum of (dish base price + extras prices) * quantity per order line
Order confirmation email is sent with total price

method_breakdown.summary: Creates order with full token validation, duplicate check, guest acceptance enforcement, line persistence, and email notification
parameters: orderLine (OrderLineCTO[]): List of dish + extras order lines
bookingToken (String): CB_ or GB_ prefixed token
method_breakdown.returns: Promise<Order>: Persisted order with populated relations
method_breakdown.significance: Primary order creation with all business rule enforcement

files.summary: NestJS use case for cancelling bookings with expiration date validation and cascade deletion.
files.description: Handles the booking cancellation workflow by validating the booking token, checking the cancellation time window against the booking's expiration date, performing cascade deletion of invited guests and orders, and sending cancellation emails to host and all guests.
business_rules: Booking must exist for the provided token; throws InvalidTokenException otherwise
Cancellation is only allowed if current time is before the booking's expirationDate
If cancellation window has passed, throws InvalidCancelationTimeException
All invited guests are cascade-deleted when a booking is cancelled
Cancellation email notifications are sent to the host and all invited guests

method_breakdown.summary: Validates token, checks time window, cascade-deletes booking and guests, sends cancellation emails
parameters: token (String): The booking token starting with CB_
method_breakdown.returns: Promise<void>
method_breakdown.significance: Enforces cancellation business rules and performs complete cleanup

files.summary: NestJS use case for finding an available restaurant table for a given date and party size.
files.description: Implements the table assignment algorithm for common reservations. Searches for free tables within a 1-hour window before the booking date with sufficient seating capacity for the party. Returns the first available table's ID or undefined if no tables are available.
business_rules: Table search window is from (booking date - 1 hour) to booking date
Table must have seats >= number of assistants (party size)
Returns the first available table (no preference weighting)
If no free table exists, booking creation fails with NoFreeTablesException

method_breakdown.summary: Queries for available tables with sufficient capacity in the booking time window
method_breakdown.returns: Promise<number | undefined>: Table ID or undefined if none available
method_breakdown.significance: Ensures a table is available before confirming a reservation

files.summary: Angular service handling booking creation HTTP calls and booking data composition.
files.description: Provides the Angular frontend interface for posting new table bookings to the backend REST API. Composes booking request payloads based on booking type (common reservation vs. group invitation) and handles invited guest email list mapping.
business_rules: Booking type 0 indicates a common table reservation requiring number of assistants
Booking type 1 indicates a group invitation requiring a list of guest email addresses
Invited guests are mapped from plain email strings to {email} objects

method_breakdown.summary: Sends booking creation request to the backend REST API
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<BookingResponse>: Response with booking confirmation
method_breakdown.significance: Main booking submission API call

method_breakdown.summary: Constructs the booking payload object based on type: adds assistants for common or guest emails for invitation
method_breakdown.returns: Booking: Composed booking request model
method_breakdown.significance: Adapts form data to backend API contract

files.summary: Angular service for fetching filtered dish data and composing menu order items.
files.description: Provides Angular frontend services for the menu page, including dish retrieval with filtering (categories, search text, max price, min likes, sorting) and conversion of menu dish views to order model objects. Maintains category name to server ID mapping for filter translation.
business_rules: Category names map to server IDs: mainDishes=0, starters=1, desserts=2, noodle=3, rice=4, curry=5, vegan=6, vegetarian=7, favourites=8
Sort parameters are cleared if no sort property is specified
Each dish added to order gets a unique UUID as local identifier
Initial order line amount defaults to 1 with empty comment

method_breakdown.summary: Fetches paginated dish list with filters from backend
parameters: filters (Filter): Category, search, price, likes, pagination filters
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<{pageable, content}>: Paginated dish list
method_breakdown.significance: Core menu data loading operation

method_breakdown.summary: Translates frontend filter form data to backend API filter format with category ID mapping
method_breakdown.returns: Filter: Backend-compatible filter object
method_breakdown.significance: Bridges frontend filter UI state to backend search criteria

method_breakdown.summary: Converts a selected dish view into an order model ready for the order cart
method_breakdown.returns: Order: New order item with UUID, dish, extras, amount=1
method_breakdown.significance: Entry point for adding dishes to the shopping cart

files.summary: Angular service for the waiter/manager cockpit providing order and reservation management data.
files.description: Supplies the waiter and manager cockpit views with order and reservation data from the backend. Supports filtered and unfiltered order searches, reservation searches, and price calculation for order summaries.
business_rules: Orders can be filtered by email or booking token for targeted lookup
Unfiltered order search does not include email or bookingToken in the request
Total price is calculated using the shared PriceCalculatorService

method_breakdown.summary: Fetches orders from backend with optional email/token filter and pagination
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<OrderResponse>: Paginated order list
method_breakdown.significance: Primary data feed for waiter order management view

method_breakdown.summary: Fetches bookings with pagination and sorting for the reservation cockpit
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<BookingResponse>: Paginated reservation list
method_breakdown.significance: Primary data feed for reservation management view

method_breakdown.summary: Calculates total price for a list of order lines including extras
parameters: orderLines (OrderView[]): List of order view items
method_breakdown.returns: number: Total price
method_breakdown.significance: Used to display order totals in cockpit

files.summary: Angular service managing the order cart side panel including order submission with booking token.
files.description: Manages the shopping cart side navigation panel state and order submission. Retrieves the current order list from NgRx store, composes the backend order payload with booking token, and submits orders to the REST API. Controls side panel open/close state.
business_rules: Orders must include a booking token to be submitted
Extras are mapped to ID-only objects for the backend API
Side nav is automatically closed when orders are submitted

method_breakdown.summary: Reads current cart from store, composes order payload with token, and posts to backend
parameters: token (String): Booking token for the order
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<SaveOrderResponse>: Order creation response
method_breakdown.significance: Core order submission operation linking cart to backend

method_breakdown.summary: Converts NgRx order store items into backend API order line format
parameters: orders (Order[]): Cart orders from NgRx store
method_breakdown.returns: OrderInfo[]: Backend-compatible order line objects
method_breakdown.significance: Data transformation between frontend cart model and API contract

files.summary: Shared service for calculating dish and order prices including extras.
files.description: Provides reusable price calculation logic for individual order items and total order price. Used across the menu cart view and waiter cockpit order summary.
business_rules: Line price = (dish base price + sum of selected extras prices) * quantity
Total order price = sum of all individual line prices

method_breakdown.summary: Calculates price for a single order item: (dish price + extras total) * amount
parameters: order (OrderView | OrderViewResult): Order item with dish, extras, and quantity
method_breakdown.returns: number: Calculated line total
method_breakdown.significance: Core pricing formula applied consistently across frontend views

method_breakdown.summary: Sums all order line prices for a complete order total
method_breakdown.returns: number: Total order price
method_breakdown.significance: Displays final order cost to customer and waiter

files.summary: Angular service handling user authentication, registration, two-factor setup, and password management.
files.description: Manages all user-related operations from the Angular frontend including login (JWT token retrieval), user registration, 2FA pairing via QR code, 2FA status toggle, and password change. Dispatches NgRx actions for auth state management and uses snackbar notifications for user feedback.
business_rules: Login sends credentials to the backend and expects a JWT token in the response
Registration requires username, password, and email
Two-factor pairing retrieves a QR code for TOTP authenticator setup
Two-factor status can be toggled per user
Password change requires old password for verification
Logout dispatches NgRx logout action to clear auth state

method_breakdown.summary: Posts credentials to backend login endpoint and returns HTTP response with JWT
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<any>: HTTP response with JWT token in header
method_breakdown.significance: Authentication entry point

method_breakdown.summary: Posts new user registration data to backend
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<any>: Registration result
method_breakdown.significance: New user self-registration

method_breakdown.summary: Fetches QR code data for 2FA TOTP setup for the current logged-in user
method_breakdown.returns: Observable<TwoFactorResponse>: QR code and secret data
method_breakdown.significance: Two-factor authentication enrollment
